meta.originalInput: Starting a new habit feels physically exhausting. That isn't a lack of discipline. It's surface friction. The first time you take an action, the ground resists. But each repetition carves a deeper physical groove. The edges smooth out. The furrow deepens. Over time, resistance drops to zero. You don't need endless motivation. You just need to carve the track until momentum takes over.

story.coreIdea: A repeated low-cost concession quietly alters the system baseline until an abnormal compromise becomes the new unconscious normal.
story.centralClaim: Destructive patterns do not begin with catastrophic failures; they begin with unexamined micro-compromises.
story.viewerPromise: Recognize the invisible shift where a single small concession hardens into an automatic habit.
story.viewerQuestion: How does a tiny, harmless compromise turn into an automatic habit before you notice?
